verdict.rationale: Both changes fix the December crash and the matching Q4 crash with a small rollover helper, so they behave the same for valid input. A adds regression tests for December and Q4 and reports a passing suite. B adds no tests and, as its report honestly says, ran no tests. Against that, A also routes the start date through the rollover helper. Out-of-range input such as month 13 or quarter 5 now silently becomes next year instead of raising, while B keeps that validation. A's tests still outweigh this.
a_issues: Building the start date with `_first_of_month` means `month_range(2026, 13)` and `quarter_range(2026, 5)` silently return next-year ranges instead of raising ValueError. That is a quiet loss of input validation.
No test runs `monthly_report` or `quarterly_report` for December or Q4 end to end.
b_issues: No regression tests were added, so nothing protects the December and Q4 fix.
The report says no test suite was run. Verification was limited to calling the date-range functions directly.
